scope: the minimum overlap fraction the 2026 replay binds event lineage with, and therefore whether the ambiguous-lineage refusal can occur at all

authorization.instruction: loosen the overlap rule and run again; nothing that requires human review may remain in the final production system
authorization.why_the_owner: this changes what the system means by 'the same deforestation event across two dates', which is a scientific rule and not a technical detail. The executing agent measured the consequence and escalated it rather than choosing.
authorization.escalation_source: docs/implementation/PHASE_4B_2026-09-09.md §4, which measured that 34 of 107 expected acquisitions could not be given event lineage under the frozen value

decided.applies_to: the Phase 4 replay only; the blue runtime default is untouched
decided.rule_in_words: a new detection joins an existing event only when the MAJORITY of the new detection's area lies inside that event. Below that it is a new event.

why_this_direction_and_not_the_other.the_instruction_was_directionally_ambigu: 'loosen the overlap rule' can mean requiring LESS overlap or building a LOOSER lineage graph, and the two are opposite. Measured rather than guessed.
why_this_direction_and_not_the_other.measured: a parent-child link is created only when intersection/current_area >= min_overlap_frac (src/detection/persistence.py:838-846), so RAISING the threshold creates FEWER links and therefore fewer many-to-many components. LOWERING it makes the refusal more likely, not less.

sweep.method: update_tracks called directly against real data — the state rebuilt from 2026-02-11's saved alerts, and 2026-03-13's polygons re-derived from the composite on disk. No reimplementation of the guard.
sweep.reading: the frozen 0.05 refuses; so does every value below it. The refusal clears at 0.30 and above.

why_strictly_above_one_half_and_not_the_.requirement: the owner requires that nothing needing human review remain in the final production system. 0.30 merely did not raise on the date that was measured; it is not prevented from raising on data not yet seen.
why_strictly_above_one_half_and_not_the_.structural_argument: two DISTINCT parents can each cover a fraction f of the same current polygon only if their intersections with it are disjoint subsets of it, so 2f <= 1 and f <= 0.5. For a threshold strictly greater than 0.5 a current polygon can therefore have AT MOST ONE parent. Both branches of the guard require some polygon to have more than one parent, so both become unreachable — by construction, not by luck.
why_strictly_above_one_half_and_not_the_.premise_that_argument_needs: the parents' intersections with the current polygon are disjoint, which holds when active track geometries do not overlap each other in area.

premise_measured.state: the replay's own persistence state, 5049 active tracks
premise_measured.reading: active tracks touch at boundaries and never overlap in area, so the premise holds on the measured state. 281 pairs intersect by the 'intersects' predicate, which includes touching.

why_strictly_above_one_half_and_not_the_.why_0_55_and_not_0_501: 0.55 clears the 0.5 boundary with margin against geometry and floating-point noise while keeping as much chaining as the guarantee allows, and it states a rule a reader can repeat: a majority of the new detection must lie inside the existing event.
why_strictly_above_one_half_and_not_the_.not_a_proof_of_impossibility: the structural argument is exact in real arithmetic given area-disjoint tracks. It is not a proof that update_tracks can never raise, because nothing in the producer PROMISES that active tracks stay area-disjoint; it is measured on this state. If a future state carries overlapping active tracks the argument weakens from impossible to unlikely, and that is why the guard is left in place rather than deleted.

measured_cost.what_is_lost: chaining. A higher threshold means fewer new detections are recognised as continuations of an existing event, so fewer alerts accumulate a persistence streak.
measured_cost.reading: 0.55 chains 369 of 6839 against 457 at the lowest threshold that cleared the refusal — about 19 percent fewer chained alerts than 0.30 would give, in exchange for the refusal becoming structurally unreachable instead of merely unobserved.
measured_cost.what_is_NOT_lost: no detection is discarded. Every polygon is still published; what changes is whether it is labelled a continuation of an earlier event or a new one. Compare with the frozen value, under which 34 of 107 acquisitions produced NO published alerts at all.

does_not_change.blue_default: src/detection/persistence.py DEFAULT_MIN_OVERLAP_FRAC stays 0.05, and the scheduled pipeline keeps resolving it.
does_not_change.the_guard_itself: AmbiguousLineageError is not removed and update_tracks is not modified. The threshold makes it unreachable; deleting it would remove the evidence if the premise ever failed.

what_this_does_not_settle.the_production_cutover: the blue runtime still resolves 0.05. Carrying this value into the scheduled pipeline is a Phase 6 change with its own review, and the owner's no-human-review requirement applies to it there.
what_this_does_not_settle.whether_0_55_is_the_scientifically_right: the value is justified structurally and by cost, not by validation against labelled data. Phase 5 owns that question and now has the sweep as its input.
